analysis.title: AI rebound provides opportunity to reduce concentrated exposures (UBS House View - Daily Asia)
key_insights: US stocks rebounded Monday after a steep sell-off. S&P 500 closed +4.7%, Nasdaq 100 +6.9%, and NVIDIA +31.5% after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO.

Nasdaq fell around 10% last week, its largest weekly decline since March 2020, and ended Friday 19.8% below its 6 October high, near bear market territory. S&P 500 lost 8.6% last week and is about 11.5% below its 6 October high.

UBS does not see the volatility as a break in the structural AI investment story. Cloud growth, rising usage and compute demand remain supportive, but it expects more differentiation between platforms with visible monetization and debt-dependent or capacity-scarce names.

Global and US equities stay Neutral on elevated expectations, concentrated leadership and AI monetization uncertainty. Holding exposure near strategic allocation is advised, with a balanced portfolio at about half equities and tech about one-third of that.

Use the rebound to cut overlapping US megacap tech exposure. UBS favors the Eurozone (similar earnings growth to the US, lower valuations), industrials and health care, and US equal-weight strategies.

Within AI, prefer established platforms, compute, leading foundries and selected semiconductor-equipment names. Be cautious on leveraged capacity providers and earnings exposed to weaker capex, normalizing prices or poor utilization.

Rebalance into fixed income with intermediate duration of about 2 to 10 years. Select high yield and EM bonds yielding 7-8% offer the most compelling return potential but carry equity-like sensitivity.

Gold stays Attractive with a forecast of USD 5,000/oz by December 2027. Gold fell 9% last week and rebounded 3% to USD 3,636/oz. Diversified commodities including copper and macro, market-neutral and fixed income RV hedge funds are also favored.

Copper fell more than 18% from its September record and briefly dipped below USD 12,000/t before rebounding. UBS stays positive on constrained mine supply (Antofagasta, First Quantum, BHP), depressed China TCRCs and electrification demand. It favors long copper or selling downside volatility near term.

Brent has fallen 21.3% in November, on course for its first monthly decline in five months, as Middle East exports recovered to about 19.5 mb/d in October. UBS says this is not a normalization and expects oil supported in 1H 2027.

Asia policy steadied markets: Taiwan tightened short-selling limits, mainland China eased margin financing, and South Korea flagged stabilization measures. The Taiwan index rose more than 2% while KOSPI stayed lower.

risk_factors: AI monetization uncertainty and the shift in focus from capex scale to returns.
Debt-funded and capacity-scarce AI names are exposed to weaker capex, normalizing prices or poor utilization.
Higher US real yields, dollar strength and liquidity-driven selling pressuring gold.
Renewed Gulf shipping attacks and uncertainty over how long US military protection continues.
Higher yield and EM bonds carry credit risk and equity-like sensitivity.
vol_and_positioning: Holiday-shortened US week and reduced liquidity ahead of Thanksgiving may amplify index swings in either direction.
LME copper net-long positioning has declined and prices are oversold. UBS favors selling downside volatility in copper near term, acknowledging downside price risk.
Hedge fund allocation to macro, market-neutral and fixed income RV is recommended for diversification when stocks and bonds move together.
geopolitical: Iran reported two oil tankers struck mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, one catching fire, following US strikes on a missile launch site on Qeshm Island.
19 confirmed attacks on ships occurred in the first 18 days of November, and US naval escorts support the recovery in Gulf exports.
Asia authorities intervened with Taiwan short-selling limits, China margin-financing easing and South Korea stabilization pledges.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud growth, rising usage and compute demand remain supportive, and the rebound shows strong dip buying.
tension_points.bear_case: Focus has shifted from capex scale to returns, with Nasdaq down about 20% from its high and concentration and debt-dependent names exposed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weakening in rates of AI investment, compute demand, financing conditions or the revenue to free cash flow to investment relationship, the factors UBS says it watches before changing its tactical stance.
